newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian 10-yr bond back eyeing the peak.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian 10-yr bond back eyeing the peak.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract ended the
SYCOM session firm, leaving scope for another attack on the all
*June, Q2 retail trade data due 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT)

The Australian 10-year bond futures contract ended the SYCOM session firm, leaving scope for another attack on the all time peak of 93.640, and a level that was left unscathed after Wednesday's brief rate cut rally.
The contract ended after hours trade at 93.575, up from Wednesday's 93.515 pit close.

Peter Pontikis, technical strategist said the reality of the Wednesday's 1/2 point rate cut to 5.0 percent by the Reserve Bank will put pressure on the 93.630/93.650 area, although it may need the front end of the yield curve to lead the way.

The 10-year bond quickly recoiled to the psychological 93.500 level after jumping to 93.630 on the easing announcement as the move had been anticipated, and analysts are now pondering whether this will be the last in the current cycle.
Howver, a strong rally in U.S. Treasuries on Wednesday helped the market find a firm footing again.

The U.S. market saw a broad brush of buying interest amid no signs of accelerating inflation, decreased supply following a federal budget deal and a strengthening U.S. dollar, push the 30-year bond yield down to a 1-1/2 year low of 6.32 percent.

The local focus will be on the June and second quarter retail trade data at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), and an address by Treasurer Peter Costello to the Economic Society in Melbourne at 2.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).

Median forecasts centre on a monthly 0.4 percent rise after the 2.9 percent increase in May, while quarterly growth is seen at 0.1 percent after 2.2 percent in the first quarter, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
